title: The rule of 72
summary: Divide 72 by a yearly growth rate to estimate how many years it takes to double. It works for savings, inflation and debt alike.
evidenceNote: The rule of 72 is a mental-math approximation that works best for rates between roughly 4% and 12%. Investment returns are never guaranteed — this is an explanation, not financial advice.

scenes.text: There's a two-second trick for how fast money grows.
Divide 72 by the yearly growth rate. That's roughly how many years it takes to double.
At 7% a year, 72 ÷ 7 ≈ 10. The money doubles in about a decade.
It's because growth compounds: each year's gains start earning gains of their own.
